title: Production Observability Stack — OTel Collector, Prometheus & Loki
exp: Architect full-stack observability pipelines using OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus Alertmanager, and Grafana Loki.
pts: **OpenTelemetry Collector:** Receiver → Processor (memory limiter, batch) → Exporter (Prometheus, OTLP/Jaeger).

qa.q: Why is OpenTelemetry Collector preferred over agent-specific metrics exporters?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** The OTel Collector provides a vendor-neutral proxy that decouples application code from monitoring backends, allowing you to route, filter, batch, and re-export metrics/logs/traces to Prometheus, Datadog, or Jaeger without changing application code.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Serverless/managed services eliminate infrastructure maintenance but introduce cold starts and vendor lock-in.

qa.q: How does Grafana Loki achieve massive cost savings compared to Elasticsearch/Kibana for logs?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Loki does not index log line full text; it only indexes log metadata labels (e.g., service, env), storing compressed log chunks directly in object storage (S3/GCS), dramatically reducing storage and CPU costs.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Indexes store data in B-Tree structures. Clustered indexes dictate physical row storage on disk leaf pages; non-clustered indexes point to clustered keys or RIDs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Over-indexing degrades write performance on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations and leads to index fragmentation and page splits.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Covering indexes eliminate costly Key Lookups for read-heavy workloads but increase storage footprint and write transaction overhead.
